description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” of various multilingual BERT models—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across different language families and isolates, as evaluated in the context of morphosyntactic probing. The horizontal axis categorizes languages into groups: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, and Uralic, with an additional unlabeled gray bar between “Isolate” and “Uralic.” The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to over 30, with major gridlines at intervals of 10. Each language group contains up to six colored bars representing the different models, with error bars indicating variability. For example, in IE-Indic, mBERT-R₂ (light green) and XLM-R₂ (dark green) show high effects (~20–23), while mBERT-B₂ (pink) and XLM-B₂ (red) also perform strongly (~22–23). In contrast, for Uralic, most models show near-zero effect, with only XLM-B₂ (red) showing a small positive value (~1–2). The IE-Slavic family shows high performance for mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ (both ~15–17), while IE-Germanic shows moderate performance across most models (~10–15). The “Isolate” category shows generally low effects across all models, mostly below 3. The chart visually emphasizes that performance varies significantly by language family and model, with some models (like XLM-B₂ and mBERT-B₂) consistently performing better in certain families (e.g., IE-Indic, IE-Slavic), while others (like mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂) show more moderate or inconsistent results. The legend on the right identifies each model by color and subscript notation (L₂, R₂, B₂), indicating different training or architectural variants.
